_what: Transparent rule tables for soc-resolver.mjs. Every rule here is a model-judgment (a human-readable keyword rule written for this mode), not a record. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries. No LLM is called at run time.

degree._degree_and_high_school_patterns: DEGREE_RE and HS_RE in soc-resolver.mjs (bachelor's/BS/BA/undergraduate/4-year/college/advanced/master's/associate degree; 'degree in'; high school diploma; GED)

soc_rules.why: a project-manager title is the 13-1082 Project Management Specialists core case
a non-technical program-manager title is usually filed with project-management work
a supply-chain project/program title can be filed as Logisticians or as Supply Chain Managers (11-3071.04)
when the text describes technical/system program work the role can be filed as IT Project Manager (15-1299.09) or Computer & Information Systems Manager
analyst/planner titles listed as 13-1081.02 Logistics Analysts alternates
a Planner title can be Logisticians (job zone 4) or the clerical Production, Planning & Expediting Clerks (job zone 2)
purchase-order and buying duties are Purchasing Agents work
a supply-chain/logistics manager title can be 11-3071 (incl. .04 Supply Chain Managers)
business-operations titles appear as 13-1111 Management Analysts alternates (e.g. Business Operations Analyst)
an operations-manager title can be General and Operations Managers
business-operations text that leads projects/programs can be filed as project-management work
coordinator/expediter titles can fall under the clerical 43-5061 code

spread._why: 10,000 USD or 10% between candidate medians is roughly one OEWS wage-level step for these occupations — wide enough that the SOC choice, not the job, sets the wage floor. 0.05 composite is a quarter of the scorer's Consider band width (0.20–0.30). Both are your-input thresholds, declared here and in the recipe; change them here, never in code.

onet_hints._why: which O*NET detail row to read job zone and cognitive_pivot_score from when a rule names a 6-digit SOC; wages always come from the 6-digit BLS row
